implementation_notes: Express has no authentication of its own, but its middleware chain is the enforcement point: app.use('/api', passport.authenticate('jwt', { session: false })) guards everything under the mount path and the strategy (passport-jwt, passport-local, an OIDC strategy) is the swappable mechanism. Middleware order is the policy - anything mounted before the guard is public - so the guard belongs on the router, not inside individual handlers; Fastify's equivalent is a preHandler hook. Passport callbacks that continue on failure are the classic fail-open trap, so make the challenge explicit for APIs.
pitfalls: Middleware registered after a route does not protect it: order and mount paths define the protected surface, so mount the guard on the router before its routes are declared.
Relying on passport.authenticate defaults for APIs produces redirects or silent fall-through; pass the failure mode explicitly and answer 401 with WWW-Authenticate.
